'''Fabricio Raúl Jesús Oberto''' ({{IPA|es-419|faˈβɾisjo oˈβeɾto|lang}}; born March 21, 1975) is an Argentine-Italian<ref name="euroleague.net">[http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=AJE&seasoncode=E2003 Euroleague.net OBERTO, FABRICIO Nationality: Italy.]</ref><ref name="acb.com">{{Cite web |url=http://www.acb.com/jugador.php?id=A4H |title=ACB.com F. Oberto nacionalidad{{!}}licencia: ITA |access-date=2012-02-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120523182525/http://www.acb.com/jugador.php?id=A4H |archive-date=2012-05-23 |url-status=dead }}</ref> color analyst and former professional [[basketball]] player. At {{height|ft=6|in=10}}, he played as a [[Center (basketball)|center]] and [[power forward]]. With the [[Liga Nacional de Básquet|LNB]] club [[Asociación Deportiva Atenas|Atenas]], in his native Argentina, Oberto began playing professionally in 1993, and later played overseas with teams in Spain and Greece. In 2005, Oberto signed with the [[San Antonio Spurs]], a team of the American [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), and won a championship with the Spurs in [[2007 NBA Finals|2007]]. He is also a former member of the senior [[Argentina national basketball team]], with whom he won two Olympic medals, including a gold medal [[Basketball at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|in 2004]].

He was inducted into the [[List of members of the FIBA Hall of Fame|FIBA Hall of Fame]] in 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|title=2019 Class of FIBA Hall of Fame: Fabricio Oberto|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/news/2019-class-of-fiba-hall-of-fame-fabricio-oberto|website=FIBA.basketball|access-date=2020-05-03}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Argentina and Europe===
At age 17, Oberto went to a trial at [[Asociación Deportiva Atenas|Atenas de Córdoba]], one of the most important basketball clubs in Argentina, and was selected to start the following year, and started playing professionally later that year. In 1998, after being chosen [[Liga Nacional de Básquet Awards|MVP of the finals]] of the [[Liga Nacional de Básquetbol|Argentine league]], he transferred to the [[Greek Basket League|Greek League]] club [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]],<ref>{{cite web | url=https://lariojabasquet.wordpress.com/2013/01/04/fabricio-oberto-vuelve-a-la-liga-nacional/ |title=Fabricio Oberto vuelve a la Liga Nacional|work=La Rioja Basquet |date=2013-01-04 |access-date=2014-06-08|language=es}}</ref> starting his [[EuroLeague]] experience that would take him to the [[Liga ACB|Spanish League]]'s [[Saski Baskonia|Tau Cerámica]] a year later. After 3 seasons with TAU, he moved to [[Valencia Basket|Pamesa Valencia]] in 2002.

He was selected to play in 4 Argentine All-Star Games (1995–1998), winning the slam dunk contest in 1995.<ref>[https://www.acb.com/jugador/trayectoria-logros/id/20200458 Fabricio Oberto - acb.com]</ref>

===NBA career===
In 2005, after voiding his contract with Pamesa, Oberto signed a three-year, [[United States dollar|US$]]7.5 million contract with the [[San Antonio Spurs]] of the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]], where he joined fellow [[Argentina|Argentine]] [[Manu Ginóbili]]. He kept with jersey number 7, the same kit number he used with the [[Argentina national basketball team]]. Oberto was the oldest rookie in Spurs history at the age of 31.<ref name="nbabio">[http://www.nba.com/playerfile/fabricio_oberto/bio.html NBA.com: Fabricio Oberto Bio Page] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090101184219/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/fabricio_oberto/bio.html |date=2009-01-01 }}</ref>

During his first year in the NBA, Oberto usually averaged fewer than nine minutes per game.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Fabricio Oberto|url=https://stats.nba.com/player/101177/|access-date=2020-10-07|website=NBA Stats}}</ref> Still, he was satisfied with his role on the Spurs as a perennial championship contender.

In his second NBA season, Oberto became more of a factor in the Spurs rotation, starting in some games and getting his first double-double on November 8, 2006, when he scored 22 points and pulled down 10 rebounds.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20120305170606/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=261108024 Spurs respond in OT after Duncan misses late FTs]</ref> He also became a pivotal player for the Spurs during the 2006–07 Western Conference Finals, averaging 31 minutes and 14 points in the first two games of the series.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sportsline.com/nba/story/10197603 |title=San Antonio Spurs, Andres Nocioni, Carlos Boozer, Carlos Delfino, National Basketball Association - CBS SportsLine.com |access-date=2007-05-26 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070528062552/http://www.sportsline.com/nba/story/10197603 |archive-date=2007-05-28 }}</ref> Oberto won an NBA championship with the Spurs in 2007.

On June 23, 2009, Oberto was traded to the [[Detroit Pistons]] as a part of a three-team trade among Pistons, Spurs and the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], which included [[Richard Jefferson]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/oberto_090623.html |title=Pistons Acquire Fabricio Oberto in Three-Team Trade with San Antonio and Milwaukee |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=2009-06-23 |access-date=2009-06-24}}</ref> Then he was immediately waived by the Pistons.

On August 11, 2009, he was signed by the Wizards.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/wizards/news/oberto_090811.html |title=Wizards Sign Fabricio Oberto |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=2009-08-11 |access-date=2009-08-12}}</ref> Since jersey number 7 was already taken by [[Andray Blatche]], he chose to wear number 21 because of his birth date (March 21) and in honor of one of his idols, former teammate [[Tim Duncan]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.ole.clarin.com/notas/2009/08/12/basquet/01976705.html |title=Me quieren para que los haga más inteligentes en la cancha|work=[[Diario Olé]] |date=2009-08-12 |access-date=2009-08-12|language=es}}</ref> After a single season in which he got limited playing time as the team struggled through the [[National Basketball Association criticisms and controversies#Gilbert Arenas/Javaris Crittenton gun incident|Gilbert Arenas gun incident]] and ultimately began to rebuild, he became a free agent once more in the summer of 2010.

Oberto was a significant contributor defending [[Argentina National basketball Team|Argentina]] for its fifth-place finish at the [[2010 FIBA World Championship]]. After his solid play during the World Championship in [[Turkey]], he received multiple offers from European teams, most notably [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Efes Pilsen]]<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.ole.com.ar/basquet/Oberto-Blazers_0_358164324.html |title=Oberto usa Blazer|work=[[Diario Olé]] |date=2010-10-22 |access-date=2010-10-24|language=es}}</ref> and [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]].<ref name="ole.com.ar">{{cite web | url=http://www.ole.com.ar/basquet/Oberto-quinto-Stone_0_358764205.html |title=Oberto es el quinto Stone|work=[[Diario Olé]] |date=2010-10-23 |access-date=2010-10-24|language=es}}</ref> Oberto held out for an opportunity to sign with an NBA team. He reached an agreement to join the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] for the 2010–11 season.<ref name="ole.com.ar"/><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=5716251|title=Sources: Blazers sign Fabricio Oberto|work=[[ESPN.com]]|date=2010-10-22 |access-date=2010-10-24}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2010/news/10/25/blazers_oberto.ap/index.html?ls=iref:nbahpt2|title=Blazers sign C Oberto, waive F Pendergraph|work=[[NBA.com]]|date=2010-10-26|access-date=2010-10-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121109181931/http://www.nba.com/2010/news/10/25/blazers_oberto.ap/index.html?ls=iref:nbahpt2|archive-date=2012-11-09|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.iamatrailblazersfan.com/PressReleaseDisplay/tabid/297/ItemID/1994/Default.aspx |title=Trail Blazers sign Fabricio Oberto |publisher=trailblazers.com |date=2010-10-26 |access-date=2010-10-26 |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101029041618/http://www.iamatrailblazersfan.com/PressReleaseDisplay/tabid/297/ItemID/1994/Default.aspx |archive-date=2010-10-29 }}</ref> However, on November 4, 2010, after playing five games for Portland, he began experiencing palpitations related to a previous heart condition and decided to retire in order to preserve his health.<ref>{{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20101107104147/http://www.iamatrailblazersfan.com/PressReleaseDisplay/tabid/297/ItemID/2026/Default.aspx Fabricio Oberto announces retirement]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.ole.com.ar/basquet/retira-Oberto_0_365963544.html |title=Se retira Oberto|work=[[Diario Olé]] |date=2010-11-04 |access-date=2010-11-05|language=es}}</ref>

===Return to activity===
In January 2013, Oberto signed a contract with his former team, Atenas de Córdoba, returning to the Liga Nacional de Básquetbol after 14 years. Oberto was hired for the remainder of the season as a replacement for [[center (basketball)|center]] Julián Aprea, who had been separated from the team by coach Alejandro Lotterio and then dismissed at the end of 2012.<ref>[http://mundod.lavoz.com.ar/basquet/atenas-dio-de-baja-julian-aprea "Atenas dio de baja a Julián Aprea", ''La Voz del Interior''], 27 December 2012</ref><ref>[http://www.lnb.com.ar/x7/index.php/lnb/noticiasa/item/1476-aprea "Atenas dio de baja a Aprea", LNB website] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130101075536/http://www.lnb.com.ar/x7/index.php/lnb/noticiasa/item/1476-aprea |date=January 1, 2013 }}, 27 December 2012</ref><ref>[http://mundod.lavoz.com.ar/basquet/fabricio-oberto-un-aterrizaje-galactico-en-atenas "Fabricio Oberto, un aterrizaje galáctico en Atenas", ''La Voz del Interior''], 2 January 2013</ref><ref>[http://www.clarin.com/deportes/regreso-esperado_0_839916245.html "El regreso más esperado"], ''[[Clarín (Argentine newspaper)|Clarín]]'', 2 January 2013</ref>

==National team career==
Oberto started playing with the [[Argentina national basketball team]] shortly before his 20th birthday in 1995; tournament success followed, including bringing to Argentina a gold medal at the [[Basketball at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2004 Summer Olympics]]. He additionally won a bronze medal with the team in [[Basketball at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|the 2008 tournament]].

In July 2011, Oberto announced that he was coming out of retirement to play in the [[2011 FIBA Americas Championship|FIBA Americas Championship]]. He said that doctors had cleared him to participate.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20110810214718/http://www.fiba.com/pages/eng/fc/news/lateNews/arti.asp?newsid=48284 ARG - Oberto ready to go]</ref> Personal problems prevented him from playing for Argentina in the [[Basketball at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2012 Summer Olympics]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.infobae.com/notas/649836-Fabricio-Oberto-no-ira-a-los-Juegos-Olimpicos.html |title=Fabricio Oberto no irá a los Juegos Olímpicos |access-date=July 23, 2012 |archive-date=July 3, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120703053113/http://www.infobae.com/notas/649836-Fabricio-Oberto-no-ira-a-los-Juegos-Olimpicos.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Post-playing career==
On February 9, 2021, the [[Austin Spurs]] of the [[NBA G League]] announced that Oberto would be the team's color analyst during the [[2020–21 NBA G League season|2020–21 season]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://austin.gleague.nba.com/news/2021-season-broadcast-schedule|title=Former San Antonio Spur Fabricio Oberto joins Austin Spurs broadcast team|date=2021-02-09|website=NBA.com|accessdate=2021-02-09}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Oberto was born in [https://getblock.me/u/27568616 Las Varillas], Argentina. Oberto and his wife have a daughter.<ref name="nbabio" /> He also enjoys playing the guitar and his favorite bands include [[Pearl Jam]], [[Nirvana (band)|Nirvana]], [[Foo Fighters]], [[U2]] and [[Metallica]].<ref name="nbabio" />

On June 4, 2009, Oberto underwent a successful ablation procedure to correct the electrical system of the heart that was sending Oberto into [[atrial fibrillation]]. The procedure was performed at the Texas Cardiac Arrhythmia Institute in Austin.<ref>{{cite web |title=Fabricio Oberto Medical Update |url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/oberto_medical_update_090608.html |website=NBA.com |access-date=September 16, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090612025423/http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/oberto_medical_update_090608.html |archive-date=June 12, 2009 |date=June 8, 2009}}</ref>
